_about: Field cards for minerals on mine dumps, used by the app's mine spot guide. Keys are lower-case mineral names as they appear in USGS MRDS ore/gangue lists. look = how to spot it, test = quick field check, care = handling caution, uv = fluorescence. Hazard facts: US Forest Service, Wyoming DEQ, Colorado Geological Survey, Arizona State Mine Inspector, EPA (sources below). Mineral properties: standard mineralogy (Mindat). Fluorescence: uvminerals.org and CAMEO.

look_for: Work the waste piles, not the workings. The dump is what the miners threw away, which is often exactly the crystals and colourful minerals collectors want.
Break open pieces of white quartz and look in cavities (vugs) for crystals and metallic flecks.
Green and blue stains (copper), rusty boxwork (weathered sulphides) and heavy-for-their-size rocks are all worth a closer look.
Look along the edges and toe of the pile and in fresh slumps after rain: weathering washes the surface clean.
aware: Never enter a tunnel (adit) or go near a shaft: old workings collapse, flood and fill with bad air, and shaft openings can be hidden under rotten boards or brush.
Don't dig into or climb steep dump faces: waste rock slides. Stay off fine tailings and settling ponds, which can be soft and deep.
Old mine waste can hold lead, arsenic, mercury and other metals: wear gloves, don't eat on the pile, wash hands and finds, and keep kids and dogs off fine tailings.
Leave old explosives, blasting caps, cables and machinery alone: they become unstable with age.
Old mines often sit on patented (private) or active claims: check land status and get permission.
general.bring: Gloves, safety glasses, rock hammer, hand lens, a magnet, a white streak plate (unglazed tile), a shortwave UV light for night hunting, bags and a marker.

quartz.look: Glassy, white to clear (purple = amethyst, smoky = brown); six-sided crystals in cavities.
quartz.test: Scratches glass; breaks with curved (conchoidal) surfaces, no flat cleavage.

pyrite.look: Pale brassy-yellow metallic cubes or striated grains: 'fool's gold'.
pyrite.test: Hard (a knife barely scratches it), brittle, greenish-black streak; real gold is soft and bends.
pyrite.care: Breaks down in damp air into sulphuric acid ('pyrite rot'): store specimens dry.

marcasite.look: Paler than pyrite, in spear or cockscomb shapes, tarnishes quickly.
marcasite.care: Decays faster than pyrite into acid and white powder; keep dry and away from other specimens.

chalcopyrite.look: Deeper brassy-yellow than pyrite, often with a blue-purple iridescent tarnish. The main copper ore.
chalcopyrite.test: Softer than pyrite (a knife scratches it), greenish-black streak.

bornite.look: 'Peacock ore': bronze on a fresh break, quickly tarnishing purple, blue and red.
bornite.test: Soft, grey-black streak; the tarnish rubs off to bronze.

chalcocite.look: Dark lead-grey, sooty-looking copper ore, often with green copper stains nearby.
chalcocite.test: Soft and sectile: a knife shaves it.

covellite.look: Deep indigo-blue metallic plates, often iridescent purple.
covellite.test: Very soft, thin flakes bend; turns purple when wet.

malachite.look: Bright green crusts, often banded in light and dark green. Copper carbonate.
malachite.test: Fizzes in a drop of acid (vinegar slowly); pale green streak.
malachite.care: Copper mineral: wash hands, don't sand or grind it dry.

azurite.look: Deep blue crusts or small crystals, often with malachite.
azurite.test: Fizzes in acid; light blue streak.

chrysocolla.look: Sky-blue to blue-green, soft and earthy, often coating rock or mixed with quartz.
chrysocolla.test: Soft (a knife scratches it) and porous; hard, glassy blue pieces mixed with quartz are 'gem silica'.

cuprite.look: Dark red, glassy to earthy, often with native copper or green malachite around it.

copper.look: Copper-coloured metal, often in wires or flattened sheets with a green or black coating.

tetrahedrite.look: Steel-grey metallic, sometimes in small triangular-pyramid crystals; often carries silver.
tetrahedrite.care: Can contain antimony and arsenic: wash hands.

galena.look: Lead-grey, shiny, breaks into perfect little cubes. Very heavy.
galena.test: Heft it (surprisingly heavy), cubic cleavage, grey streak, soft.
galena.care: Lead ore: don't lick or grind it, wash hands, keep from kids and pets.

cerussite.look: White to grey, very bright (diamond-like) lustre, sometimes in six-rayed twinned crystals.
cerussite.test: Unusually heavy for a white mineral; fizzes slowly in acid.
cerussite.care: Lead carbonate: same care as galena.

sphalerite.look: Resinous yellow, brown, red or black ('rosin jack', 'black jack'). The main zinc ore.
sphalerite.test: Pale yellow-brown streak even from black pieces; many shiny cleavage faces.
sphalerite.uv: Some sphalerite glows orange or blue under UV.

smithsonite.look: Bubbly (botryoidal) crusts in pale blue, green, pink or brown. Zinc carbonate.
smithsonite.test: Heavy for a crust; fizzes in warm acid.

calcite.look: White to clear, breaks into slanted rhombs.
calcite.test: Scratched by a knife, fizzes in a drop of acid.
calcite.uv: Fluoresces in many colours (red, orange, blue, white) depending on the mine: worth a UV check.

siderite.look: Tan to brown rhombic carbonate, weathering rusty.
siderite.test: Heavier than calcite; fizzes only in warm acid.

ankerite.look: Cream to buff carbonate that weathers rusty brown, common in gold-quartz veins.
ankerite.test: Weak fizz in acid, browns on exposure.

dolomite.look: White to pink rhombs, often with curved 'saddle' faces.
dolomite.test: Fizzes only when powdered or in warm acid.

barite.look: White to tan, bladed or tabular crystals.
barite.test: Feels far too heavy for a light-coloured mineral; soft (a knife scratches it).

fluorite.look: Purple, green or yellow cubes; breaks into octahedra.
fluorite.test: Scratched by a knife but scratches calcite.
fluorite.uv: Usually glows blue-violet under longwave UV.

scheelite.look: White to tan, heavy, greasy-looking grains or crystals in quartz or skarn. Tungsten ore.
scheelite.uv: Glows bright blue-white under SHORTWAVE UV: hunt the dump at night with a shortwave lamp.

wolframite.look: Black to dark brown, bladed, very heavy. Tungsten ore.
wolframite.test: Heavy, one perfect cleavage, dark brown streak.

molybdenite.look: Soft lead-grey hexagonal flakes with a greasy feel, often in quartz.
molybdenite.test: Marks paper like pencil lead but bluish; thin flakes bend.

stibnite.look: Lead-grey, long striated needle or blade crystals.
stibnite.care: Antimony mineral: wash hands, don't heat.

arsenopyrite.look: Silver-white metallic, often in wedge-shaped crystals; tarnishes yellowish.
arsenopyrite.test: Gives a garlic smell when struck with a hammer.
arsenopyrite.care: ARSENIC: don't hammer it near your face, avoid the dust, wash hands and keep it away from food.

pyrrhotite.care: Decays into acid in damp storage.

magnetite.look: Black metallic grains or eight-sided crystals.

hematite.look: Red-brown earthy masses or shiny steel-grey ('specular') flakes.

limonite.look: Rusty yellow-brown earthy coatings and boxwork: the weathered cap over sulphide veins ('gossan').
limonite.care: A sign of weathered sulphides below: the metals came from somewhere.

gold.look: Buttery yellow that stays bright in shade and from any angle, never tarnishes.
gold.test: Soft and malleable (dents with a pin), very heavy; pyrite and chalcopyrite are brittle and darker.

silver.look: Silver-white wires or flakes that tarnish black.

argentite.test: Cuts like lead with a knife.

stephanite.look: Black metallic silver-antimony ore, short prisms.

pyrargyrite.look: Dark red 'ruby silver' with a bright lustre.
pyrargyrite.care: Darkens in light: store specimens in the dark.

garnet.look: Rounded 12- or 24-faced crystals: red-brown in schist, green-brown in skarn.

epidote.look: Pistachio-green prisms and crusts, common in altered rock and skarn.

tourmaline.look: Black striated prisms with a rounded-triangle cross-section (schorl).
tourmaline.test: Hard, no cleavage, no flat ends.

cinnabar.look: Bright red to scarlet, earthy or crystalline. Mercury ore.
cinnabar.care: MERCURY: never heat it, wash hands, keep away from food.

serpentine.look: Greasy green, smooth or scaly rock.
serpentine.care: Fibrous serpentine (chrysotile) is ASBESTOS: don't break or carry fibrous pieces, avoid the dust.

chalcedony.look: Waxy, translucent white, grey or blue quartz without visible crystals; banded = agate.
chalcedony.test: Scratches glass; waxy lustre and curved fracture.

adularia.look: Clear to milky, glassy feldspar crystals with a rhomb-like shape, typical of epithermal gold veins.
adularia.test: Hard (about 6), two cleavages at right angles; can show a soft blue sheen (moonstone).

electrum.look: Pale yellow to whitish gold-silver alloy in specks and flakes.
electrum.test: Soft and malleable like gold, but paler.

sylvanite.look: Silver-grey metallic blades or skeletal crystals: a gold-silver telluride ore.
sylvanite.test: Very soft, one perfect cleavage, grey streak.

gypsum.look: Clear to white, soft crystals or fibrous seams; clear crystals are selenite.
gypsum.test: A fingernail scratches it; thin pieces bend.

selenite.look: Clear, glassy gypsum crystals or plates.

graphite.look: Black-grey, greasy flakes in schist or marble.
graphite.test: Marks paper black like a pencil; feels greasy.

wulfenite.look: Thin square orange, yellow or red plates. Lead molybdate.

pyromorphite.look: Bright green to yellow-brown six-sided barrels. Lead phosphate.

rhodochrosite.look: Rose-pink to red carbonate, banded or in rhombs.

hemimorphite.look: White to pale blue fans of thin blades or bubbly crusts. Zinc silicate.

amethyst.look: Purple quartz crystals, often in vugs.
amethyst.test: Scratches glass; colour can fade in strong sun.

beryl.look: Six-sided prisms: pale green, blue (aquamarine) or yellow, in pegmatite.
beryl.test: Very hard (scratches quartz), flat ends on crystals.

realgar.care: ARSENIC sulphide and it crumbles in light: don't handle much, wash hands, store in the dark.

orpiment.look: Lemon to golden yellow, soft, pearly flakes.
orpiment.care: ARSENIC sulphide: don't handle much, wash hands.

autunite.care: URANIUM mineral, radioactive: leave it, don't carry it.

willemite.look: White, green or brown grains or prisms, usually in zinc ore.
willemite.uv: Often glows bright green under shortwave UV.

muscovite.look: Silvery, glittering flakes that peel into thin sheets (mica).

biotite.look: Black or dark brown mica flakes.

tremolite.look: White to grey-green long blades or silky fibres, often radiating sprays in marble or altered rock.
tremolite.test: Hard (scratches glass), two cleavages at about 56 and 124 degrees. Fibrous forms look like silky hair.
tremolite.care: Fibrous tremolite is asbestos. Don't break, scrape or bag fibrous pieces; leave them and move on.

actinolite.look: Dark to bright green long prisms or needles, sometimes radiating; common in greenschist and skarn.
actinolite.test: Hard, green, two cleavages at 56/124 degrees. Nephrite jade is a tough, felted form of it.
actinolite.care: Fibrous actinolite is asbestos: leave fibrous material alone and don't break it.

chrysotile.look: Silky, flexible green-gold to white fibres in veins through serpentine rock.
chrysotile.test: Fibres pull apart like silk thread; sits in veins cutting across green serpentine.
chrysotile.care: This is the common form of asbestos. Look, photograph, don't touch, break or collect.

uraninite.look: Black, heavy, pitchy lumps or tiny cubes, often with yellow or green crusts of secondary uranium minerals.
uraninite.test: Very heavy for its size, black streak. Yellow-green crusts nearby (autunite) glow green under UV.
uraninite.care: Radioactive. Don't keep specimens indoors or in a pocket, don't grind it, wash your hands. Check rules: some old uranium sites are closed.

sericite.look: Fine, silky, pale mica that makes altered rock feel soapy and look bleached and shiny.
sericite.test: Too fine to see flakes; the rock is soft, pale and silky. Marks hydrothermal alteration around ore.

chlorite.look: Dark green, soft flaky mineral; makes rock green and soapy, often coating other crystals.
chlorite.test: Soft (fingernail scratches it), green flakes bend but don't spring back like mica.

anglesite.look: Colourless, white or grey glassy crystals or crusts around weathered galena.
anglesite.test: Very heavy for a clear mineral, sits on or around galena; often yellow-fluorescent under UV.
anglesite.care: Lead mineral: wash hands, don't lick or grind.

talc.look: White, pale green or grey, very soft and greasy-feeling masses.
talc.test: Softest mineral: your fingernail scratches it easily and it feels like soap.

boulangerite.look: Lead-grey, fine hair-like or feathery needles, sometimes felted masses.
boulangerite.test: Metallic grey needles, heavy, grey-black streak. Hard to tell from jamesonite by eye.
boulangerite.care: Lead-antimony mineral: wash hands, don't grind.

jamesonite.look: Dark lead-grey needles or feathery tufts ('feather ore').
jamesonite.test: Metallic, brittle needles, grey-black streak, heavy.
jamesonite.care: Lead-antimony mineral: wash hands, don't grind.

bournonite.look: Steel-grey metallic stubby crystals, sometimes twinned like cogwheels.
bournonite.test: Metallic grey, heavy, brittle; the cogwheel twins give it away.

chromite.look: Black, heavy, granular grains or pods in serpentine and dark rock.
chromite.test: Brown streak (magnetite's is black), weakly magnetic at most, heavy.

ilmenite.look: Black, heavy, slightly metallic grains or plates; common in black sand.
ilmenite.test: Black to brown-red streak, weakly magnetic; tells black-sand concentrate from magnetite.

diopside.look: Pale to bright green stubby glassy prisms in marble and skarn.
diopside.test: Hard, near-square cross-section, two cleavages near 90 degrees.

feldspar.look: White, pink, cream or grey blocky crystals with flat shiny cleavage faces.
feldspar.test: Hard (scratches glass), two cleavages at about 90 degrees, flat faces flash in the sun.

zircon.look: Small brown, red or clear four-sided crystals with pointed ends; tiny grains in black sand.
zircon.test: Very hard, bright lustre, square cross-section; many glow yellow under shortwave UV.

apatite.look: Green, blue, yellow or brown six-sided glassy prisms.
apatite.test: Knife scratches it (hardness 5), six-sided; some glow under UV.

rutile.look: Red-brown to black shiny needles or striated prisms, sometimes golden needles inside quartz.
rutile.test: Very bright lustre, pale brown streak, striated lengthwise.

magnesite.look: White, porcelain-like or grainy masses, often in serpentine.
magnesite.test: Like white chalky china; fizzes only in warm acid (calcite fizzes in cold).

hübnerite.look: Red-brown to black bladed crystals, often in quartz veins.
hübnerite.test: Heavy, red-brown streak, one perfect cleavage. Tungsten ore, a form of wolframite.

proustite.look: Ruby-red translucent crystals ('ruby silver'), darkening in light.
proustite.test: Scarlet streak, very heavy for its size, soft. Keep in the dark.
proustite.care: Arsenic-silver mineral: wash hands, store away from light.

powellite.look: Yellowish, cream or grey crusts and tiny crystals on molybdenite.
powellite.test: Glows bright yellow under shortwave UV, which is the easy way to find it.
